messages:
support-alex: FYI customer org=acme-io is seeing intermittent 429s since 08:12 UTC but the Quota panel in Console shows ~85% remaining. Raised a ticket, customer is escalated and blocked on a critical flow.

liam-sre: thanks for flagging. Do we have request_ids or example request headers? Need to check enforcement-service vs billing rate limiter.

support-alex: pasted samples from customer logs: `req_id=01F8XY9A user=svc-api token=tok_live_org_123 status=429 code=rate_exceeded` Also sending one curl repro I used:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer tok_live_org_123" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
They hit 429s after ~120 requests/minute. Console -> Quotas shows limit 600/min, usage 90 so should be fine.

amar-eng: pinging quota-bot and the enforcement logs now. @quota-bot can you paste enforcement decision for these req_ids?

quota-bot: enforcement-log: {"time":"2026-02-12T08:13:04Z","org":"acme-io","limit_key":"per_min:org:acme-io","limit":100,"current":101,"decision":"reject","backend_node":"enf-13","policy_version":"v3.4.1"}

liam-sre: aha — enforcement-service shows a limit of 100/min not 600/min. That mismatch explains the 429s. Need to know why Console is showing 600. Two hypotheses: (1) config drift during config service rollout, (2) Console reading cached policy from older datastore.

jess-pm: customer-facing impact is high. Who owns config publish pipeline? @amar-eng and @ops-kim can you triage root cause and timeline to patch? We should also tell the customer expected ETA.

amar-eng: running direct query against config-store (postgres primary): `SELECT org, limit_key, limit_value, updated_at FROM org_quota_policies WHERE org='acme-io';` returns limit_value=100 updated_at=2026-02-11T23:02:12Z.

ops-kim: console cache layer uses a daily rollup and a TTL of 6h for org-level policies (was introduced in rollout 2025-11). Looks like the config published to enforcement-service but the console cache was not invalidated. Console shows the cached 600/min record from earlier. Enforcement is correct at 100.

liam-sre: root cause = cache invalidation bug in console cache invalidator -> missed delta events during config publish when event payloads were trimmed. We saw similar symptoms in prod 2025-12 but fixed for global policies; org-level path missed.

support-alex: next steps: 1) tell customer we found root cause (config drift due to cache invalidation) 2) change enforcement to relax back to 600 temporarily? That could be risky. 3) fix console cache invalidator ASAP and backfill cache.

amar-eng: I propose: apply hotfix to cache invalidator to pick up trimmed events (deploy prefixed branch `cache/invalidate-org-delta`) -> roll out to staging, then prod. Meanwhile I'll run a one-off admin mutation to sync console cache for acme-io so their UI reflects 100 (or after actions, 600 if we choose).

ops-kim: we should NOT change enforcement limits on-the-fly. That risks over-provisioning and violating org contracts. Recommend fix console only and optionally offer customer transient rate bump (manual override) if they accept.

jess-pm: I'll coordinate comms. Support: tell customer we're investigating, root cause identified (console stale cache), ETA for hotfix 2h, option for manual override if they need immediate relief.

liam-sre: repro steps for engineers: 1) publish org quota update via admin API: `POST /admin/orgs/acme-io/quota {limit:600}` 2) check kafka topic `config.deltas` for trimmed payloads using: `kcat -b kafka:9092 -t config.deltas -o beginning | jq 'select(.org=="acme-io")'` 3) observe console cache TTL and missing invalidation event. 4) enforcement-service reads from policy-store directly and will apply latest policy immediately.

amar-eng: I'm starting the hotfix branch now and will open a PR + run through staging. I'll also create a short script to backfill the console cache for affected orgs: `python tools/backfill_console_cache.py --org acme-io`.

support-alex: customer update sent with ETA and manual override offer. I'll mark ticket high-priority and post follow-up once cache sync or hotfix is live. :thumbsup:

liam-sre: logging follow-up: add a temporary alert if enforcement limit != console policy for any org for >5m. That will prevent silent drift. Filing infra ticket INF-4231.

ops-kim: noted, will add to runbook and coordinate postmortem.

support-alex: closing loop here — will post final status when resolved.
